currentContext.business: Alkem is a Mumbai-headquartered diversified healthcare company built on a domestic branded and trade-generics prescription pharma franchise (housed under wholly-owned subsidiary Alkem Wellness), leading in acute and chronic therapies such as anti-infectives, vitamins and nutrients, pain management and gastro-intestinal, with growing presence in anti-diabetics, dermatology, urology, ophthalmology and respiratory care. Its international business spans regulated and emerging markets across the United States, Europe, Australia, Latin America, CIS, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia through own products, subsidiaries and partnerships. It is also building newer platforms in MedTech (orthopaedics and, via a proposed Occlutech investment, structural-heart/cardiovascular devices), biosimilars and Bio-CDMO (Enzene Biosciences), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (Alkem Activa), and consumer wellness (ActivLife).

Consumer Health (ActivLife): A-to-Z brand portfolio (nutrition, women's health, paediatric care, everyday wellness)
MedTech: orthopaedic implants and surgical solutions (Advita Ortho, erstwhile Exactech; Alkem Medtech Ortho, erstwhile Bombay Ortho)
Biotech: Bio-CDMO development and manufacturing (New Jersey, USA)

currentContext.end_markets: India|United States|Europe (incl. Western Europe)|Australia|Latin America|CIS region|Middle East|Africa|Southeast Asia|Japan (new MedTech entry geography via proposed Occlutech transaction)

currentContext.strengths: Domestic prescription business ranks among India's largest, with leadership across acute and chronic therapies (anti-infectives, vitamins & nutrients, pain management, gastro-intestinal)|International platform spanning more than forty countries combining own products, strategic partnerships and market-specific capabilities|Dense distribution network: 8,800+ stockists and 14,500+ medical representatives in India|Regulatory and R&D track record: 192 cumulative ANDA filings and 2 NDA filings with USFDA, 1 BLA filed, 3 dedicated R&D centres with 595+ scientists|Manufacturing scale and quality accreditation: 20 plants worldwide (5 USFDA-approved) with UK MHRA, EMA, TGA and WHO clearances
currentContext.strategies: US strategy prioritises innovative/complex generics, including oral oncology and injectable products, with additional focus on biosimilars, as the US market shifts toward innovation and speciality products|International emerging-markets strategy: replicate successful execution models from CIS and the Middle East across scalable markets, strengthen growth momentum in Africa, and restore performance in Southeast Asia through improved regulatory sequencing and focused launches|Expand selectively into B2C (direct-to-consumer) branded generics businesses across new geographies|Continue investing in regulatory, quality and operational capabilities to support the emerging-markets platform|Enzene Biosciences pursuing dual-platform biologics strategy: a commercial biosimilars business serving India (with select assets out-licensed globally) and a CDMO business serving domestic and international clients via India and US (Enzene Inc.) facilities|Enzene international biosimilars expansion via a capital-efficient out-licensing model, where Enzene develops and manufactures while regional partners handle in-country registration and commercialisation, generating milestone and royalty revenue|The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy states it is deeply committed to driving superior value creation for all stakeholders and believes driving growth creates maximum shareholder value; it therefore first deploys profits to fund working-capital requirements, capital-expenditure requirements, reducing debt, and allocating reserves for inorganic growth opportunities, and only thereafter distributes surplus profits as dividend to shareholders.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 capital deployment centred on three new growth platforms rather than core-plant capacity addition. In MedTech, Alkem MedTech executed a binding term sheet (13 Feb 2026) to acquire a 51-55% controlling stake in Occlutech Holding AG, a Swiss structural-heart device specialist, alongside continued integration of Advita Ortho (erstwhile Exactech) and the newly acquired Bombay Ortho (renamed Alkem Medtech Ortho). In Biosimilars, Enzene Biosciences continued investment in capacity expansion, manufacturing readiness and international commercialisation, with its biosimilar portfolio approaching European launch readiness and US out-licensing opportunities evolving (Enzene's US Hopewell, New Jersey facility commissioning and Denosumab/Pertuzumab milestones are detailed in the strategy_outlook domain). In GLP-1, the Company strengthened manufacturing readiness and expanded strategic international partnerships to support launch and scale-up of its GLP-1 portfolio in India. Behind these, a digital-infrastructure build-out (Project EKAM, SAP HANA 2023, Project Aspire, and Level-2 MES integration across facilities) now supports a unified platform used by 22,000+ users. Management states the Occlutech investment (like the MedTech and Biosimilars investments generally) is being funded through internal accruals and existing cash, with no new debt and no equity dilution.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
